children: The National Bank of Poland (NBP) is expected to keep interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, a Reuters poll showed, with analysts pointing to rising inflation and loose fiscal policy as reasons for caution.
All 29 respondents in a Reuters poll forecast the NBP would keep its main rate (PLINTR=ECI) at 3.75% in September.
Inflation rose to 3.4% on the year in August, more than expected by analysts, nearing the top end of the central bank's target range of 1.5% to 3.5%.

It was the fastest pace of consumer price growth in more than a year, driven mainly by the rising cost of fuel after the expiry of a government program meant to keep down prices, as oil prices surged after the Israeli-U.S. attack on Iran.

"In July, the NBP governor signaled a possibility of rate cuts, but in light of recent inflation developments and taking into account the sharp rise in long term yields, we think this time the policy message will be more cautious," Citibank analysts wrote in a note.
"In particular, the central bank head may point towards a persistently high fiscal deficit as one of the potential factors limiting room for rate cuts."
A draft budget for 2027 projected the general government deficit to GDP ratio to remain unchanged next year at 7.1%, and ease only marginally from 7.3% in 2025.

NBP Governor Adam Glapinski said in July he could propose a 25-basis-point interest rate cut after the summer, adding though that other Monetary Policy Council members could prove more cautious about further monetary easing.
The bank last cut interest rates in March.
